label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Hi Tolu, I'm in Biology 100L right now and I applied for Medicine and Surgery, so this is literally my story. I'll tell you everything I know, the good and the not so good, because you asked for honest.

**My own gist first**

I wrote JAMB in 2025 and scored 251. I applied Medicine and Surgery in a federal uni here in Lagos and got offered Biology. The day I saw Biology on that portal, I locked myself inside my cousin's room in Surulere and cried. I didn't eat that day. So when you say you've been crying since afternoon, I understand you well well. It's not dramatic. You had your mind fixed on one thing and it didn't happen, so it's normal to feel like that.

The part that pained me pass was that my mum was still telling people in church that I'm doing Medicine. For like two months o. I had to beg her to stop because every time someone congratulated me I wanted the ground to open. If you have that kind of pressure at home, I see you.

**Can you actually transfer? Yes, but hear me well**

Kingsley said transfer is a myth. That's not true. Favour said just read hard and you'll transfer. That's too simple. The truth is somewhere in between and it's not as sweet as Favour made it sound.

This is what our level adviser told us in my school (please note, MY school, I'll come back to this):

- You need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5 after 100L to even be considered for transfer to MBBS.
- Even with 4.5, there must be space. If Medicine is full, it's full. Your CGPA alone doesn't carry you in.
- You also need to have met the Medicine cut-offs in both JAMB and post-UTME. So it's not only about how you do in 100L. They look back at your entry scores too.
- Last year, she said about 6 people were moved in from the whole faculty. Not the department, the whole faculty. She thinks over 40 applied.

So I want you to sit with that. Around 6 out of 40+. People do make it. It's real. But it's a small door and plenty people are pushing at it.

About your 268: I don't know your school's Medicine cut-off for JAMB or what your post-UTME score was, so I can't tell you if you're eligible. Please don't assume 268 means you're fine. Check both: the JAMB cut-off for Medicine in your school AND your post-UTME score against what Medicine needed. If you fell short on either one, transfer might not even be open to you no matter how well you do in 100L, at least going by how my school does it. That's something you need to know BEFORE you pay acceptance fee.

**Where I am now**

I won't lie to you. My CGPA after first semester is 4.31. Not 4.5. I'm still pushing, I haven't given up, but I'm telling you so you know it's not "just read hard" kind of thing. I read. I'm still reading. 100L is tougher than people make it sound.

The courses in 100L are BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and Maths are the ones dealing with people, honestly. If you're not strong there, that's where your CGPA can drop and you won't even know how it happened. BIO and CHM are more manageable if you're serious. So if you go the transfer route, start working on Physics and Maths from day one. Don't wait for test.

Also small practical thing, it costs money: lab coat was 6,500 naira, dissecting kit was 9k, and practical manual is extra. Just so your dad knows.

**Is Biology a bad course? Honestly, no**

This one surprised me. I entered Biology feeling like I was wearing someone else's shoe. Then our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, lol. I was fine. And that day I realised I actually like this thing. Like genuinely.

Now I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I ever expected. Biology is not a dustbin course like some people make it seem. It's real science and there's plenty you can do with it. I still want Medicine, I'm not going to pretend I don't, but I don't feel like I'm wasting my life in Biology anymore. Those are two different feelings and both are true for me.

So to your question "is it that Biology is bad or that I had my mind on Medicine," for me it was the second one. The disappointment was about Medicine, not about Biology itself.

**About rewriting**

I'm not going to tell you rewriting is wrong. It's not. If you're ready, it can work. But staying at home is not as easy as people say.

My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times since then. She's still at home. I'm not saying that to scare you. She's brilliant and I'm sure she'll get in. But "one year is nothing" is easy to say when you're not the one sitting at home while your mates are in school. One year can become two, and the post-UTME is not guaranteed even if your JAMB is high, because you already had 268 and still didn't get Medicine this time.

If you're going to rewrite, ask yourself honestly: what will I do differently this time? Will I be okay emotionally at home for a year? What if it doesn't work the second time? If you have good answers, then rewriting is a valid choice.

**What I'd actually do if I were you, with two weeks left**

1. **Go to the faculty or your department physically and ask the exact transfer rules for YOUR school.** What CGPA? Is it after first year only? Do they check JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs? How many people moved last year and how many applied? Don't just trust forum people, and that includes me. My school's rules might be different from yours. Get it from the horse's mouth before your deadline.

2. **Check your JAMB and post-UTME scores against Medicine's cut-offs in your school.** If you didn't meet them, then accepting Biology "to transfer" might not make sense, and that changes everything.

3. **Ask yourself one question quietly, by yourself, not with your dad or aunty in the room:** Do I want Medicine, or do I want to be "doctor" for my parents? It's not a bad question, no shaking. Some people truly want it and that's fine, then fight for it. But some of us (me included at some point) were half chasing the title because of family and church people. Knowing which one it is for you will help you decide whether to fight hard, rewrite, or open yourself up to something else.

4. **If you accept Biology, accept it with your eyes open.** Not thinking transfer is automatic. Go in planning to work hard for it, but also giving Biology a chance. You might like it like I did. And if transfer doesn't happen, you're not stranded. There are other paths, including Medicine later through other routes, or other careers in health and science.

**Last thing**

Whatever you choose, it's not the end of the world. I promise you. A year ago I was crying in Surulere thinking my life had scattered. Now I'm here dissecting toads and enjoying genetics and still fighting for my transfer. I'm okay. You'll be okay too.

You already did well. 268 is not small. You're not a failure because the portal said Biology. Take a deep breath, go and ask your school the real questions, and then decide from facts, not from fear and not from what everybody is shouting in the comments (including me again lol).

If you want to ask me anything else about 100L, drop it here. I'll reply. Rooting for you, Tolu.

– Amaka
